subject: Logic
title: Precautionary Principle
description: A short lesson to help you apply Precautionary Principle.

hook.text: A new chemical seems safe—but long-term effects are unknown. Should you wait for proof of harm or proof of safety?

buildup.text: The precautionary principle: when potential harm is severe and irreversible, act cautiously even without full proof.

discovery.text: It shifts the burden of proof—instead of proving danger, we demand proof of safety before proceeding.

twist.text: Critics say it blocks innovation. Taken to extremes, nothing new would ever be approved.

climax.text: The key is proportionality: apply extra caution only when potential harms are catastrophic and irreversible.

punchline.text: When the stakes are permanent, caution is rational.

quiz.question: When does the precautionary principle apply?
options: When potential harm is severe and irreversible
